_comment_family: ITC American Typewriter ships as a family — Light through Bold, with
condensed widths beside them — and every one of those files carries
'American Typewriter ITC Pro' as name ID 1, with the cut in the
subfamily. Asking for that family alone would let any of them answer,
and this face is used as a highlight against a Forma DJR ExtraBold:
the whole point of it is that it is the heavy slab, so a Light
answering in its place would leave a picked word LIGHTER than the
words around it, which is the emphasis backwards.
So the full name (name ID 4) is what gets declared, the same way
gilroy-extrabold and the two Telegraf packs declare theirs.

_comment_stack: Every other face in this folder falls back through Impact and Arial
Black, and this one must not: those are heavy grotesques, and what
makes this face a highlight is that it is a SLAB SERIF — a change of
voice rather than of weight. A fallback that dropped the serifs would
leave a picked word looking like the block it was meant to stand out
from, which is a failure that draws no attention to itself.
So the fallbacks are the nearest slabs a Windows machine can be
relied on to have: American Typewriter itself where it is installed,
Rockwell where Office put one there, and Courier New — which is on
every Windows there is and is at least a typewriter — before the
generic serif. All of them are still wrong metrics and fontguard
still fails the channel over a missing file; this only decides what a
